summary.headline: Bajaj Auto Q2 FY27 revenue crossed INR20,000 crore (+34% YoY) and EBITDA INR4,172 crore at a 20.9% margin, despite 3-3.5% of revenue in new input-cost inflation.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly volumes above 1.5 million (+20% YoY), revenue of INR20,126 crore-equivalent standalone milestone (INR20,000 crore-plus), EBITDA of INR4,172 crore and PAT of INR3,354 crore (+35% YoY). Margin held at 20.9% (up 40 bps YoY) as calibrated pricing, a favourable rupee (realised INR95.5/USD) and higher other operating income offset hyperinflationary input costs of roughly 3-3.5% of revenue in Q2, on top of about 4-4.5% in Q1. Exports hit a record 7.8 lakh units (+41% YoY) and electric volumes nearly 2 lakh units. Management flagged that October rupee realisations are below 95.5 and that only about 30% of estimated Q3 inflation has been priced in so far.

financial_highlights.change: +37% YoY; margin +40 bps YoY, flat QoQ
+60% YoY, inflated by Bajaj Mobility AG (KTM) consolidation with one-quarter lag

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Record 7.8 lakh units (+41% YoY), second straight quarter above 7 lakh; revenue nearly USD800 million, about 40% of revenue. 2W export market share rose from 44% in FY26 to 48% in H1; 3W share from 60% to 63%.

segments.name: Domestic 2-wheelers / Pulsar
segments.commentary: New Pulsar 125, Pulsar 150 Classic and upgraded Pulsar 160 launched; new launches were 33% of 125cc+ portfolio in the first 16 festive days, up from 7% in August. Management conceded Classic/125cc lines are still a drag as channel stock is flushed; 100cc segment deliberately deprioritised on price.

segments.name: Probiking (KTM and Triumph)
segments.commentary: 40,000 units in Q2 (+31% YoY); H1 at 80,000 units, highest ever H1. Triumph about 11,000 units with availability impaired up to 20%. 120 KTM-Triumph showrooms operational.

segments.name: Electric (Chetak and E3W)
segments.commentary: Combined EV 2W and 3W volumes near 2 lakh units, more than double YoY; about 34% of domestic revenue (about INR5,500 crore in H1) and over 20% of enterprise revenue. Chetak market share 23% despite supply constraints; September retail about 45,000 units. EV business is EBITDA-positive and accretive to domestic margin, but dilutive to enterprise margin.

segments.name: 3-wheelers
segments.commentary: Record quarterly volume of 1.62 lakh units (+13% YoY). About 90% share in CNG passenger, over 50% in cargo, about 32% in e-autos (September). Demand exceeds capacity by about 10%.

segments.name: Spares and BGO
segments.commentary: Spares crossed INR2,000 crore quarterly revenue for the first time (+15% YoY); Bajaj Genuine Oil posted record volume and higher royalty income.

segments.name: KTM (Bajaj Mobility AG)
segments.commentary: H1 revenue EUR701 million (+65% YoY); EBITDA EUR38 million versus a loss of over EUR180 million a year earlier; Q2 EBIT positive for the first time since restructuring.

segments.name: BACL (financial subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Total income nearly INR1,200 crore; PAT INR243 crore (+85% YoY); AUM nearly INR21,000 crore; CRAR about 19.5%; ROE 26%.

guidance_outlook: Input-cost inflation is continuing into Q3 (third consecutive quarter); steel and copper are firm. Management said the magnitude is hard to quantify, but a couple of percentage points is possible if current trends hold for the full quarter.
About 30% of the estimated Q3 inflation has been recovered through a price increase in early October; management will not price to offset short-term currency moves.
October rupee realisations are below 95.5, a headwind for Q3 if sustained.
Export run-rate target of about 7.5 lakh units per quarter (240-260k per month); management will not push beyond this until retail and freight conditions improve.
Festive season (Sep-Dec) 2W industry growth expected in double digits, below the 18% of April-August. Early festive VAHAN registrations +10%; Bajaj comparable +32% in the first 16 days.
PLI effective rate for EV revenue at maximum 18% (16% base plus 2% booster) for H2 FY27; PLI scheme runs to 31 March 2028.

Chetak capacity to rise to 80,000 units per month by Q4 (currently about 60,000-64,000); overall capacity of 6.25 lakh units per month to rise to about 7.75 lakh over 6-9 months; about 75 new Chetak exclusive stores planned for Q3.
capex_capacity: Overall capacity of 6,25,000 units per month to expand to about 7,75,000 units per month over the next 6-9 months, in phases.
Chetak capacity at about 60,000-64,000 per month now, rising to 80,000 by Q4; a new site is being considered for further expansion.
Chetak exclusive stores at 550-plus, with a target of about 1,000 in 12 months; 75 of the 100 planned Q3 openings may become operational, with some slipping to January.
E3W demand exceeds capacity by about 10%; ICE and EV 3W capacity expansion is underway. 3W network grew from about 900 stores in FY23 to over 1,600.
EV plans were delivered only to about 75% of the original plan because of supply chain and component constraints.
demand_pricing: Domestic 2W industry grew 18% YoY in April-August, driven by 150cc+ motorcycles and EV scooters. Early festive VAHAN registrations +10%; 150cc+ and EV scooters +24%; Bajaj +32%.
Price increase in 100cc (M1/M2 segment) taken ahead of competition to protect margin, accepting volume loss; management says this dampens 2W volumes.
Price action in October covered about 30% of estimated Q3 inflation; the earlier Q1-Q2 pricing covered 50-60% of inflation.
Rural and entry demand is weak (K-shaped demand). Monsoon deficits in Maharashtra, southern states and the Northeast may hit Q4.
Adventure and high-performance street bikes are about 7% of the motorcycle market and growing 4x faster. Africa retail in Nigeria about 30,000 units AVPM, with a market share near 60%.
E-scooter penetration is about 25% of the scooter category, with the industry growing 75%+ in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why does VAHAN and SIAM share not show the benefit of Pulsar refreshes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 100cc segment (where volume was deliberately given up) and the Classic and 125cc lines are dragging share. The 150cc+ N and NS series (60% of the portfolio) are growing faster than the market; the Classic series launched in September and channel stock is still being flushed.

qa_highlights.question: What EV revenue split is there, and how sustainable is PLI income beyond the scheme?
qa_highlights.answer: Electric revenue was about 34% of domestic revenue, close to INR5,500 crore in H1. H2 PLI accruals should stay at the 18% maximum rate. The scheme runs to 31 March 2028; management is working on platform cost reductions to offset part of the lost PLI benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Are EV margins accretive, and what is the export incentive rate?
qa_highlights.answer: EV margins were accretive to domestic margins in Q2 thanks to the top-slab PLI, but dilutive to the 21% enterprise margin. Export incentives are 3-4% of revenue; the increase is driven by scale rather than a rate change.

qa_highlights.question: What was the October price hike and is more coming?
qa_highlights.answer: One round of pricing was taken in early October, covering about 30% of the estimated quarterly inflation (assuming a couple of points of inflation). Further pricing will depend on market absorption; currency weakness will not be priced in.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for rural demand given the weak monsoon?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% of sales come from the secondary (small-town) network. Drought-like conditions in several states may hit Q4 more than Q3; the K-shaped demand pattern is expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: How should exports and electrification be seen going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management looks at absolute volume (target 7.5 lakh per quarter) rather than growth rates; new segments, new countries and KTM joint products are the growth levers. EV exports are a small early-stage effort (Nepal, Sri Lanka); capacity is prioritised for domestic demand.

risks_watch: Hyperinflation in steel, copper, electricals, proprietary parts and conversion costs; only about 30% of estimated Q3 inflation priced in so far.
Rupee: October realisations below 95.5, a near-term margin headwind.
PLI scheme exhausts 31 March 2028, and it currently contributes a material part of EBITDA; mitigation depends on cost cuts and post-PLI pricing.
Chetak supply constraints (September delivered 40,000 against a 60,000 plan) and an ambition to become number one in EV 2W.
Pulsar channel destocking of old Classic and 125cc lines, and 100cc volume loss, which may keep domestic 2W share soft through Q3.
Export volumes need a run-rate of 7.5 lakh per quarter, and freight-driven retail price rises could affect demand; Q3 and January are seasonally weak.
Monsoon and rural stress may weigh on entry-level demand in Q4.
key_quotes: It was a festival of records in Q2, 5 of them at the corporate level, highest ever volumes, revenue, EBITDA, PAT, and free cash flow.
So, the drag was the Classic and the 100cc.
It's really difficult to pin down a number for the inflationary impact at this stage.
But if these levels were to persist, it would clearly be a bit of a headwind that we need to be able to manage for the current quarter
But in exports, there is no singular rate of growth in the market.
So, I would like to say that our goal is to keep doing 7,50,000.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, exports and the EV and KTM turnaround, with specific figures given freely. Noticeably cautious on the outlook: management would not quantify Q3 inflation, said October rupee realisations are below 95.5, and declined to guide beyond a 7.5 lakh export run-rate. It also conceded the Pulsar Classic and 125cc lines are still a drag on share.

growth.why: Management guides overall capacity from 6.25 lakh to about 7.75 lakh units/month over 6-9 months and Chetak to 80,000/month by Q4, with exports held at a 7.5 lakh/quarter goal, but festive 2W growth is guided to slow to double digits versus 18% in Apr-Aug and Q3 input inflation is only 30% priced in.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Margin held at 20.9% (+40 bps YoY) but Q3 inflation is only about 30% priced in against a possible couple of points of cost headwind, and October realisations are below 95.5, so the margin is more likely to be squeezed than to expand.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Overall capacity is being expanded from 6.25 lakh to about 7.75 lakh units per month (+24%) over 6-9 months in phases, and Chetak goes to 80,000 per month (+25%) by Q4 FY27 from about 60,000-64,000.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Festive 2W industry growth is guided to double digits (vs 18% in Apr-Aug), Bajaj comparable is +32% in the first 16 festive days, exports are targeted at 7.5 lakh per quarter (record 7.8 lakh in Q2), and Chetak demand exceeds supply, but rural and 100cc volumes are weak.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management is already expanding overall capacity by about 24% and says a new Chetak site is being considered; 3W demand exceeds capacity by about 10%, so further capacity announcements are likely.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to guide beyond the 7.5 lakh export run-rate, would not quantify Q3 inflation, and flagged October rupee realisations below 95.5.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 inflation could reach a couple of percentage points with only about 30% priced in, October realisations are below 95.5, and monsoon deficits may hit Q4 rural demand, with festive growth slowing to double digits from 18%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Pulsar 125, Pulsar 150 Classic and upgraded Pulsar 160 launched recently (new launches 33% of 125cc+ portfolio in the first 16 festive days), and about 75 new Chetak exclusive stores are planned for Q3.

rows.label: PLI top-slab EV incentive drops off after March 2028
rows.why: The PLI is at the 18% maximum for H2 FY27 and contributes a material part of EBITDA, and management is working on platform cost cuts to offset the lost benefit.

rows.label: KTM-Triumph (Probiking) volume and EBITDA turnaround
rows.why: Probiking Q2 volume was 40,000 units (+31% YoY), KTM H1 EBITDA was EUR38 million versus a loss over EUR180 million a year earlier, and Q2 EBIT was positive, although Triumph availability is constrained by up to 20%.

rows.label: Further price hikes to recover Q3 inflation
rows.why: Only about 30% of the estimated Q3 inflation is priced in versus 50-60% covered in Q1-Q2, but further pricing depends on market absorption and the 100cc segment has already lost volume.

tone.note: Management was confident on volumes, exports, EV and KTM turnaround, but cautious on the outlook: it would not quantify Q3 inflation, flagged October rupee realisations below 95.5, and conceded Pulsar Classic and 125cc lines are a drag on share; analysts pushed on share loss versus VAHAN and on PLI
